draft.title: The burden and standard of proof
card: the duty to prove the case. In a criminal trial it rests on the prosecution, not the accused.
the accused is treated as innocent until the prosecution proves guilt. The accused does not have to prove innocence.
how strongly the case must be proved. The prosecution must prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt.
If the court has a reasonable doubt about guilt, the accused must be found not guilty. Proof beyond reasonable doubt is a higher standard than the one used in civil cases.
draft.remember: The prosecution must prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt, so the accused need not prove innocence.

a.q: In a Victorian criminal trial, which side must prove the case, and to what standard?
opts: The prosecution, to prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt
The defence, to prove innocence beyond reasonable doubt
The prosecution, to show guilt is more likely than not
The defence, to raise some doubt about the evidence
a.why: The burden sits with the prosecution because the accused is presumed innocent. The standard is beyond reasonable doubt. Showing guilt is only more likely than not is too low a standard for a criminal trial.
a.clue: The accused is presumed innocent, so who must do the proving?

b.q: Jaya is tried by a jury in the County Court of Victoria for armed robbery of a service station in Footscray. The jury thinks she probably did it but still has a reasonable doubt. What should the verdict be?
opts: Not guilty, because the standard of proof was not met
Guilty, because the jury thinks she probably did it
Not guilty, because Jaya proved she was innocent
Guilty, because Jaya chose not to give evidence at trial
b.why: Probably guilty is not enough. The prosecution must remove reasonable doubt, so a jury with such doubt must find her not guilty. Jaya did not have to prove anything, so the options 'Jaya proved she was innocent' and 'Jaya chose not to give evidence' both wrongly put the burden on her.
b.clue: Does the jury's doubt mean the standard has been met?

a.best: The prosecution, to prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt

b.best: Not guilty, because the standard of proof was not met

proposal.title: Burden and standard of proof
card: the duty to prove the case. In a criminal trial it rests on the prosecution, because the accused is presumed innocent. The accused does not have to prove innocence.
how strongly the case must be proved. In a criminal trial the prosecution must prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt.
If the jury or magistrate is left with a reasonable doubt about guilt, the accused must be found not guilty. Thinking the accused probably did it is not enough.
This is higher than the civil standard, the balance of probabilities, which only asks whether a claim is more likely than not.
proposal.remember: Any reasonable doubt about guilt means a not guilty verdict, and the accused never has to prove innocence.
